MIND. [1] [Cadm. s.]
Mostly unconscious. θ Cholera infantum.
   

SENSORIUM. [2] [Cadm. s.]
Vertigo ; room and bed seem to spin around. θ Yellow fever.
   

SIGHT AND EYES. [5] [Cadm. s.]
Blennorrheic affection of eyes.
Idiopathic chronic torpid conjunctivitis.
Swelling of conjunctiva remaining after blennorrhœa.
Macula corneæ (after removal of a fragment of iron which caused inflammation) covering half the pupil, bluish, much impeding sight. θ Boy, æt. 10 years.
Macula corneæ covering pupil after a conjunctivitis and keratitis traumatica. θ Girl, æt. 6 years.
Opacity of cornea connected with slow inflammation and blennorrhœa.
Cicatrix on cornea.
Inability to close eyes. θ Paralysis of face.
   

UPPER FACE. [8] [Cadm. s.]
Pain with cold sweat in face. See 16. θ Yellow fever.
Painful drawing in face. θ Paralysis of face.
   

LOWER FACE. [9] [Cadm. s.]
Distortion of mouth to side. θ Paralysis of face.
   

TASTE, SPEECH, TONGUE. [11] [Cadm. s.]
Pitchy taste. θ Yellow fever.
Tongue shows traces of black vomit, dirty brown or black. θ Yellow fever.
Difficulty in talking and swallowing. θ Paralysis of face.
   

HICCOUGH, BELCHING, NAUSEA AND VOMITING. [16] [Cadm. s.]
Salty, rancid belching. θ Yellow fever.
Deadly nausea. θ Cholera infantum.
Intense retching and distressing nausea.
Nausea in mouth, chest and abdomen, often with pain and cold sweat in face. θ Yellow fever.
Excessive vomiting of yellowish-greenish semifluid masses, almost gelatinous. θ Cholera infantum.
Vomiting of sour, yellow and black matter, with pain in abdomen. θ Yellow fever.
Excessive nausea, gagging, retching ; so sensitive that least touch of lips will bring on vomiting. θ Yellow fever.
Deadly nausea, must lie quiet, to ward off black vomit, which is already in stomach and can he smelt. θ Yellow fever, early part of second stage.
Nausea ; or black vomit, when other medicines fail. θ Yellow fever.
   

SCROBICULUM AND STOMACH. [17] [Cadm. s.]
Burning and cutting pains in stomach. θ Yellow fever.
Useful after cramps in stomach. θ Yellow fever.
Intense burning in stomach ; also burning from œsophagus to stomach. θ Yellow fever.
   

HYPOCHONDRIA. [18] [Cadm. s.]
Lancinations in left hypochondrium. θ Yellow fever.
   

ABDOMEN AND LOINS. [19] [Cadm. s.]
Pain in abdomen, with vomiting. θ Yellow fever.
Pain and pulsation in sides of abdomen. θ Yellow fever.
Cutting pain in bowels and kidneys. θ Yellow fever.
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Cadm. s.]
Alvine evacuations, almost gelatinous, of a yellowish-green semi-fluid character. θ Cholera infantum.
   

URINARY ORGANS. [21] [Cadm. s.]
Cutting pain in region of kidney and bowels. θ Yellow fever.
   

PREGNANCY. PARTURITION. LACTATION. [24] [Cadm. s.]
Acts well during pregnancy. θ Yellow fever.
   

HEART, PULSE AND CIRCULATION. [29] [Cadm. s.]
Palpitation. θ Yellow fever.
Palpitation of heart, with constriction of chest.
   

NERVES. [36] [Cadm. s.]
Child can hardly move a limb. θ Cholera infantum.
   

SLEEP. [37] [Cadm. s.]
Can hardly sleep ; sleep, if at all, with open eyes. θ Cholera infantum.
   

TEMPERATURE AND WEATHER. [39] [Cadm. s.]
Useful if any of the grave symptoms appear after being exposed to a draught of air, or when sweat is checked. θ Yellow fever.
A man after riding in a sharp northeast wind (in France) had a half-sided rheumatic paralysis of face, apparently suddenly ; treated by the old school four weeks without success, got well in eight days after two doses of 12th.
   

FEVER. [40] [Cadm. s.]
When sweat is checked after exposure to a draught of air. θ Yellow fever.
   

STAGE OF LIFE, CONSTITUTION. [47] [Cadm. s.]
Acts well with drunkards. θ Yellow fever.
Child, æt. 15 months, teething. θ Cholera morbus.
